summary: Galbraith Mountain near Bellingham: a 12x12 ft two-story lookout built in 1942 and removed or destroyed in the mid-1950s; radio towers stand on the summit.

facts.design: 12 by 12 ft, two stories, which the sources call a "smokehouse"
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1954 per the register and FireLookout.com; Willhite says mid-1950s. The summit now has radio towers and no lookout.

access.note: Private working tree farm. Non-motorized trails are open under a recreational use agreement with the owners and a 2018 purchase agreement. Galbraith Lane is a private road with an easement, per Willhite.

visit.trail_note: Nothing to climb. Willhite says hikers can reach the summit by sticking to the road, because hiking on the mountain bike trails is forbidden.

events.note: Two-story 12x12 ft lookout, called a smokehouse, run by the Washington Division of Forestry/DNR

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says removed in 1954, FireLookout.com says destroyed in 1954, and Willhite says destroyed in the mid-1950s. The story reports all three; no source gives a more exact date.

notes_for_editor: The 1942 date and smokehouse description repeat across the register, FireLookout.com and Willhite, which may share one origin; one search found no Division of Forestry or DNR record. The brief's other_names 'Lake Samish' comes from a Mountaineers photo caption on Willhite's page. Wikipedia places the mountain between Lake Padden and Lake Whatcom, so the name may be a misattribution, but this is not proposed as a correction. Access 'restricted' is my reading of a private tree farm with public trails under agreements; check current rules before a visitor page relies on it. Read budget slightly exceeded: about eight fetches, including Wikipedia and a history blog for context.
